conventions: Distributive bab-bōqer bab-bōqer → *morning by morning* (46.13, 46.14, 46.15): both nouns are rendered, so this is not rule 22's condensation of one of them. The *by* stands before the second noun, which is where the second bə stands, so that preposition takes it and the first bə — with nothing written before the first *morning* — is `unrepresented` under rule 40. Both assimilated article tokens go `unrepresented`, the ASV writing no *the* for either noun. BSB represents the first bə in all three verses; that is the documented convention difference and not an error.

The capacity idiom yāḏ + suffix is read off what the ASV wrote, and the chapter splits it under rule 2 rather than taking it as one noncompositional unit. In the verbless mattat yāḏô (46.5, 46.11) mattat takes *to give*, yāḏ takes the discontinuous *as … is able*, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun *he* (rules 18, 40). Where a finite verb stands in the clause — kaʾăšer taśśîg yāḏô (46.7) — that verb carries *is able* under rule 44, yāḏ has no English of its own and is `unrepresented`, and the suffix still takes *he*. Each verse names the competing single noncompositional unit in its notes; BSB represents the 46.7 yāḏ.

šām: where the ASV writes one *where* for an ʾăšer … šām relative (46.20, 46.24), the relative takes it and the resumptive šām is `unrepresented` under rule 22. Where a locative šām is written in a presentative clause — wə-hinnēh-šām māqôm → *and behold, there was a place* (46.19) — that morpheme takes the written *there* and only the copula and the indefinite article join the predicate māqôm, a present morpheme taking its English before a supplied reading does, as in rules 46, 47 and 48. The competing reading takes the *there* as rule 20's construction-supplied dummy and leaves šām `unrepresented`; it is named in that verse's notes.

dereḵ + gate, nine occurrences across 46.2, 46.8 and 46.9: the ASV writes *by the way of …* throughout, so the construct never lacks an English noun of its own and rule 19's directional-construct clause (dereḵ → *toward*) is not reached anywhere in this chapter. The supplied *by* and *the* are placed on dereḵ itself as an adverbial accusative under rules 33 and 15 rather than read as rule 19's recast construct relation, and the rectum takes only the relational *of*. 46.8's suffixed darkô → *the way thereof* follows the same division.
report: Checked all 56 candidate lemma groups plus the full verse dump end to end (the table is blind to `added` units, so the six of them were read in place). No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source or in the ASV to license the difference. Verdict no-change, patches empty.

Near-misses resolved, not split: kaʾăšer fused to *as* in 46.12 but split *according* | *as* in 46.7, and ben fused with bāqār into *young* in 46.6 but split from šənātô across *a year* | *old* in 46.13. Both are rule 30's one-English-word condition met in one verse and unmet in the other, which is a difference the ASV wrote and not a split.

Articles are consistent chapter-wide after 46.17's own correction. One written *the* with the rectum rendered bare goes to the present article morpheme (46.1 yəmê ham-maʿăśeh and yôm haš-šabbāt; 46.4, 46.12, 46.17, 46.24); two written *the*s put one before each word (46.1 yôm ha-ḥōdeš; 46.2, 46.3, 46.6, 46.9, 46.19, 46.21, 46.22, 46.24). 46.1 holds both shapes and treats each correctly, and agreement articles on attributives are `unrepresented` in all three places they occur (46.1, 46.20, 46.21).

The six `added` units (46.10 *together*, 46.15 *Thus*, 46.17 *as for*, 46.20 *and* and *them*, 46.22 *cubits*) each answer to no morpheme, and no comparable supplied word is folded into a licensing morpheme elsewhere in the chapter: the waws, the kîs, the object markers and the suffixes that could have carried one all either have their own English or are marked where they do not.

BSB: 31 disagreements, all on function morphemes the ASV leaves unrendered — the frozen ʾăḏōnāy suffix, nine articles, the distributive first bə, the lə of lə-ʾarbaʿtām, the repeated tokens of 46.21's doubled clause. These are the documented convention difference and none is a genuine error. Nothing was changed to improve the rate.

Two BSB rows deserve naming rather than dismissal. 46.7 yāḏ is `unrepresented` because the finite taśśîg carries *is able* under rule 44 while 46.5 and 46.11, which write no verb, give the same noun the discontinuous *as … is able*; that is source-licensed and both verses name the competing noncompositional reading. 46.9 s043, the resumptive suffix inside the fused *whereby*, is the one accepted edge where corpus precedent reads the other way: the corpus aligns Tr+R+Sp3ms to *wherein* in 23 units with the suffix inside the unit, while this verse marks it `unrepresented` under rule 22. Left as accepted, since rule 22's text licenses it and the verse noted its reasoning; this is a rule-level question for a later pass, not a silent edit.
Four conventions recorded (the log had none). The validator's 78 repeated notes are otherwise bare restatements of rules 14, 15, 17, 19, 29 and 31 and are deliberately not logged.

No promotion. The one real candidate — amending rule 20 so a written locative šām takes the presentative *there* before the supplied dummy does — rests on a single occurrence (46.19) with no corpus evidence on how finished chapters treat hinnēh-šām clauses, so it is recorded as a chapter convention with the competing reading named instead of promoted.
